title: Inhalable Medicines for Severe Lung Diseases: Lyn Baranowski on The Long Run - TimmermanReport.com
gist: Avalyn Pharma, a Boston-based private biotech led by CEO Lyn Baranowski, is reformulating existing oral small molecules into inhalable drugs for rare severe lung diseases such as pulmonary fibrosis and other interstitial lung diseases — betting that concentrating delivery deep in the lungs allows lower doses and better long-term tolerability in an under-covered therapeutic area.

themes.theme: Reformulation over discovery: oral small molecules made inhalable

insights.claim: Avalyn Pharma's core strategy is not novel discovery but reformulation — taking a couple of small molecules already given orally and remaking them as inhalable drugs delivered deep into the lungs.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: Reformulating validated small molecules sidesteps target risk and shortens development versus de novo discovery — a cheaper shot on goal for a private biotech.
insights.locator: Avalyn has taken a couple of small molecules

insights.claim: The delivery thesis is spatial: routing the drug directly to the site of disease deep in the lungs is claimed to be more effective than systemic oral dosing for the same molecules.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: The entire value creation rests on the inhaled-delivery device and formulation, not the molecule — diligence should sit on the delivery technology.
insights.locator: so they can be more effectively delivered where they need to go

themes.theme: Dose reduction and long-term tolerability as the differentiator

insights.claim: By concentrating delivery at the target tissue, Avalyn expects to lower the doses required, which is the mechanism by which it hopes to improve tolerability.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: Lower dose plus better tolerability is the commercial wedge against incumbent oral antifibrotics known for discontinuation-driving side effects.

insights.claim: The explicit design goal is treatments patients can tolerate over the long term, framing chronic-use adherence rather than acute efficacy as the product's competitive axis.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: In chronic progressive lung disease, persistence on therapy drives lifetime revenue more than headline efficacy — tolerability data is the readout that matters.
insights.locator: make treatments that are easier for patients to tolerate

themes.theme: Rare severe lung disease as an under-covered market

insights.claim: Avalyn is targeting rare, severe lung diseases specifically including pulmonary fibrosis and other interstitial lung diseases, a defined orphan-adjacent indication set rather than broad respiratory.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: Rare severe ILD supports orphan pricing and accelerated pathways, making a small Boston-based private company plausibly acquirable.
insights.locator: developing inhalable drugs for rare, severe lung diseases

insights.claim: Respiratory disease is characterized as a therapeutic area that does not capture much news coverage even though lung diseases of one kind or another affect many people — an attention gap relative to disease burden.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: Low media and analyst attention relative to patient population is exactly where mispricing sits; screen private respiratory assets before the coverage catches up.
